## GET /admin-api/branding

`getBranding`

**This realm's sign-in appearance (#717)**

Everything Server configuration → Sign-in appearance draws: the layout and the layouts there are, the four colours and the tones derived from them, the contrast of the text, the links and the button text against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1), the display name, the logo's alternative text and link, the stored logo (its type, sides, size and digest, never its bytes), and the page's settings. `previewUrl` and `logo.src` are in this realm.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/sign-in-appearance` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

## POST /admin-api/branding/logo

`uploadBrandingLogo`

**Upload this realm's sign-in logo**

The request body is the image itself: a PNG, a JPEG or a WebP, which the bytes decide whatever `Content-Type` says. Each side 16 to 2048 pixels, at most branding.logoMaxBytes. It replaces the logo the realm had. A logo needs alternative text: send it as `alt`, or set branding.logoAlt first. Served at this realm's /web/branding/logo. Audited, with its digest and never its bytes.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/sign-in-appearance` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alt` | query | string |  | The alternative text, written to branding.logoAlt with the image. |

**Request body**

As `application/octet-stream`.

As `image/jpeg`.

As `image/png`.

As `image/webp`.

## POST /admin-api/branding/save

`saveBranding`

**Change this realm's sign-in appearance**

Writes the `branding.*` settings named, in this realm: the default realm's are the process's overrides, a realm's are its own, as `POST /admin-api/config/set` would write them. They are judged TOGETHER, so a text colour and a card colour that pass only as a pair are taken as a pair, and nothing is written when any is refused: a colour that is not one, text or links below WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1) against the card, a link that is not https, an empty alternative text while a logo is set. A key that is not one of these eight is refused by name. branding.logoMaxBytes is the process's, set with `/config/set`.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/sign-in-appearance` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branding.accentColor` | string |  | Buttons, links and focus rings, `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`; stored as six lower-case digits. |
| `branding.cardColor` | string |  | The card, `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`; stored as six lower-case digits. |
| `branding.displayName` | string |  | Shown beside the logo and in the document title. Text, never markup, and never translated. Empty for none. |
| `branding.layout` | one of `centered`, `split`, `banner` |  | centered (the card alone), split (a brand panel beside the card) or banner (a band above it). |
| `branding.logoAlt` | string |  | The logo's alternative text. Required while a logo is set. |
| `branding.logoLinkUrl` | string |  | An absolute https URL the logo links to, or empty for no link. |
| `branding.pageColor` | string |  | The page behind the card, `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`; stored as six lower-case digits. |
| `branding.textColor` | string |  | The text on the card, `#rgb` or `#rrggbb`; stored as six lower-case digits. |

**200**: The keys written, in `saved`.

**400**: The operation was refused; `errors` says why and nothing changed.

## GET /admin-api/config

`getConfig`

**Every setting this service has, and where each value came from**

Every setting, grouped by protocol, each with its effective value and the SOURCE of that value: a runtime override, an environment variable, the appconfig file CONFIG_FILE names, or `env/defaults.js` under it. The source is the part that was not answerable before this resource existed — the four are indistinguishable once a value has been read, and the question "why is the issuer that?" used to be a grep. There is no fifth source: a setting with a value in none of them stops this service from STARTING rather than falling back to a constant in a module.

It also says which settings can be CHANGED while the service runs. The ones that cannot were consumed at startup — a bound socket, the TLS certificate's names, the Kerberos principal database and its long-term keys, the directory's base DN — and each carries the reason.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/config` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The whole table.

|---|---|---|---|
| `configFile` | string, or null |  | The CONFIG_FILE this process was started with, which is the file to edit to make a change survive a restart. Nothing here ever writes to it. |
| `defaultsFile` | string |  | The DEFAULT appconfig file, which `configFile` is unioned on top of key by key with the operator's value winning. A setting whose `source` is `defaults` came from here. |
| `editableCount` | integer |  | How many of them POST /config/set will take. The rest are restart-only and say why in `restartReason`. |
| `groups` | list |  | In the order `config.js` declares them, which is the order the console renders its sections. |

## POST /admin-api/config/reset-all

`resetAllSettings`

**Drop every runtime override**

Returns the whole service to the configuration it started with, without restarting it. This is what a test should call to put the service back: the service's admin state survives between jobs, so a setting left changed here changes what every later job sees.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/config, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-settings and POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-authzen` on the admin console.

## POST /admin-api/config/set

`setSetting`

**Change one setting**

A RUNTIME OVERRIDE — the top of config.js's five layers. Whether it outlives the process is `persistence.appconfig`: with a persistent store (`persistence.mode` `ldif` or `postgres`) it is written down and re-applied at the next start through this same function, which is why it adds no sixth layer, and only with `persistence.mode=memory` is it gone on restart. A write made while a non-default realm is ambient lands on that realm and is written down with the realm row, so `persistence.realms` decides it there. The reply's `message` says which. See `GET /admin-api/persistence`.

NOTHING HERE WRITES TO THE APPCONFIG FILE in either mode, and that is deliberate rather than unfinished: a service that edited a file checked into a repository would leave a test's forgotten change behind permanently. The durable copy goes to the persistent store, which is not a place anything is checked in from.

The change applies to the next token, assertion, ticket or search. Nothing already issued changes, because a token is a signed document.

A setting whose `editable` is false is REFUSED with the reason rather than accepted, and a value that does not fit the setting's type is refused by name.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/config, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-settings and POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-authzen` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The dot path, as GET /admin-api/config lists it. |
| `value` | any JSON | yes | A string is always accepted and is coerced to the setting's type, so the environment spelling works here too; a JSON number, boolean or array of strings is accepted where the type takes one. |

**200**: The setting as it now stands, in `setting`.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | string |  |  |
| `error_description` | string |  |  |
| `errors` | list |  |  |
| `errors[]` | string |  |  |
| `key` | string |  |  |
| `message` | string |  |  |

## POST /admin-api/config/set-many

`setSettings`

**Change a whole section at once**

What the console's per-section Save posts, and it is not a convenience: a section is how a person changes configuration, and one call per field would make a partly-applied section the ordinary outcome of a mistake in any one of them.

ALL-OR-NOTHING. Every value is checked before any is written, so a body with one bad field changes nothing and names it. A key this service does not know is ignored rather than refused, because a form posts fields this resource never declared; `applied` says which were taken and `changed` which actually differed from what was already in force.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/config, POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-settings and POST /admin/xacml#xacml-tab-authzen` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

An empty object.

**200**: What was applied, in `applied`, and what actually changed, in `changed`.
